subject: Bringing together chains run separately to calculate Rhat and neff

messages.author: 9466f38039d48e25
messages.subject: Bringing together chains run separately to calculate Rhat and neff
parts:
I have a very large data set, which means I can only run one chain at a time without running out of RAM. I have access to a computing cluster, so I can run many Stan jobs in parallel on different machines, each running just one chain. Is there a best practice for bringing together these separate chains, so as to calculate Rhat (which I know is calculated across chains) and neff (which I'm not sure if it is).

I'm using Pystan, so more technically this question is really: Is there a way to combine multiple StanFit4model objects?

Thanks!
Jeff

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bringing together chains run separately to calculate Rhat and neff
parts:
The easiest way to do this is cmdstan. Try using stansummary on those files. Hopefully you won't run into RAM issues there. 

If you're offloading to a cluster, cmdstan is the way to go.

I'm using Pystan, so more technically this question is really: Is there a way to combine multiple StanFit4model objects?

Thanks!
Jeff

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bringing together chains run separately to calculate Rhat and neff
parts:
Will that rdump() function write out a data file to be used
with CmdStan? Is there something to read in a bunch of CSV files
of draws and put them together into some kind of MCMC object in
PyStan?

RStan can read in multiple CSV files produced by different
runs of CmdStan to produce an MCMC object. Currently,
all chains have to be the same number of draws, but we plan
to generalize R-hat and n_eff to varying numbers of draws.

This brings up a lot of design issues on serialization formats
that I'm going to take up on the dev list.

- Bob

On Sat, May 28, 2016 at 1:31 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Will that rdump() function write out a data file to be used
with CmdStan?
Yes, it can do that.

Is there something to read in a bunch of CSV files
of draws and put them together into some kind of MCMC object in
PyStan? ... RStan can read in multiple CSV files produced by different
runs of CmdStan to produce an MCMC object.
I have not found any such functionality yet in PyStan (though maybe others know where it's lurking). It would be nice to have!
